restitution: Yes, that is the piece: where the world's recorded wildfires are, and how the count has moved. The data is the Global Wildfire Information System's fire-count series via Our World in Data, 2012 to 2026, updated 21 August 2026.
takeaway: Africa accounts for about two-thirds of the world's recorded wildfires, and the world's count has fallen by nearly half since it peaked in 2015.
claim: None of those: it is about a share and a fall, not one maximum, minimum or comparison.
subject: Africa.
comparison: The other five continents in the same stack, and the world's own 2015 peak on the same axis.
limits: This is a count of detected fire events, not area burned, not people harmed, and not a rate. It is not comparable between countries of different size, and most of Africa's count is seasonal savanna and agricultural burning. 2026 is excluded: the dataset says the year is incomplete, last updated 21 August 2026.
placement: Under the paragraph that quotes the dataset's own description line.
credit: Global Wildfire Information System (2026), with minor processing by Our World in Data.
